App privacy policy

This policy explains what the Stuck Not Broken app keeps, why it keeps it, and how you can delete it.

Last updated: November 1, 2026

In short

The app keeps what it needs to work for you. Nothing is sold, and no advertisers see it. You can delete all of it at any time.

Who runs the app

The Stuck Not Broken app is run by Justin Sunseri, a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in California, as a sole proprietor at 924 N Yosemite Ave, Stockton, CA 95203. You can reach him about privacy at justin@stucknotbroken.com.

What the app keeps

While you have an account, the app keeps your email address. It also keeps your first name and a profile photo if you choose to add them. It keeps your check-ins, which are the three sliders and any notes you write with them. It keeps the practices you do and how they went, and your answers to lessons and journal prompts. It keeps your settings and reminders. It keeps whether you have a paid plan, which plan it is, and its dates. If you turn on notifications, it keeps the address your phone gives it for sending them. It also keeps a record of which parts of the app you use. All of this is linked to your account, and it is kept only while your account exists. When you delete your account, it is deleted too.

What the app does not collect

The app does not collect your location. If you turn on live weather, your phone sends a rough location, accurate to about 7 miles, to Open-Meteo, a weather service, so it can show you the weather. That location stays on your phone and is never sent to Stuck Not Broken. The app does not collect your contacts or your browsing history. It never sees your card number, because Apple or Stripe handles payment. There is no tracking across other apps or websites, no advertising, and no data sold to data brokers.

How it is collected

Everything above comes from what you enter in the app, or from the app noting what you use. Nothing is gathered from other sources.

Why it is kept

Your information is kept so your account works on every device you sign in from, your history is there when you come back, the app can reflect your own patterns back to you and suggest practices, reminders reach you, and the app knows whether you have a paid plan.

The anonymous copy

The app also keeps an anonymous copy of check-in and practice data. It never includes your name, your email or anything you write. It is used for two things only: learning whether the app helps people, and sharing de-identified examples of what change can look like, such as "one member's reported safety rose from 20% to 60% over six months." It is never used for advertising and never sold. While you have an account, deleting a check-in or practice also deletes it from the anonymous copy. When you delete your account, the link between you and the anonymous copy is destroyed. After that, the copy can never be connected to you again, even by Justin, and it is kept.

Apple Health

If you turn it on, the app saves your practice time to Apple Health as Mindful Minutes. The app only writes to Apple Health. It never reads your Health data, and nothing from Apple Health is used for anything else.

AI voice

Some audio in the app uses an AI voice made with Descript, and it is clearly labeled. Descript does not receive any of your information.

Who sees your information

Only you see your information, plus Justin when he needs to in order to run the app or answer a message you send him. It is not sold or shared for advertising. The following services run parts of the app and handle your information only to do that job, under their own security and privacy commitments:

  • Supabase stores the app's data and handles sign-in.
  • Circle checks your email when you sign in, to see whether you are an Unstucking Academy member.
  • Cloudflare hosts the app.
  • Apple handles App Store payments, notifications and Apple Health.
  • Stripe handles website payments.
  • Resend sends account and reminder emails.
  • Daily runs the video for live events. Live chat is not saved after an event. Some live events are recorded so attendees can watch the replay, and those events are marked as recorded ahead of time. If you turn on your camera or mic during a recorded event, the recording may include you. Recordings are only for attendees and are never shared publicly.

Your profile photo

If you add a profile photo, it appears next to your messages in live event chat. If your plan includes the community spaces, it also appears there. You can remove it at any time in Settings.

How long it is kept

Your information is kept until you delete it or delete your account. Payment records are kept as long as tax law requires. The anonymous copy is kept after your account is deleted, as described above.

Your choices

You can see your information in the app, under You and Settings. You can download your check-ins and journal in Settings, under Your data. You can delete a single check-in, or all of your data, at any time. You can turn off emails and notifications in Settings. To delete your account, go to Settings, then Leave or reset, then Delete my account. That permanently removes everything that identifies you.

Security

Your data is stored with access rules so that only your account can read it. No system is perfect. If something happens that affects your information, you will be told.

Children

The app is for people 18 and older. If Justin learns that a child has an account, it is deleted.

Your rights

Depending on where you live, such as California or the European Union, you may have the right to access, correct, delete or move your information. Write to justin@stucknotbroken.com, and you will get an answer within 30 days.

Changes

When this policy changes in a way that matters, you will hear about it in the app or by email before the change applies.
